HAP.title: Hospital-acquired pneumonia (lung infection after admission)

items: Hospital-acquired pneumonia is a lung infection that starts at least 48 hours after you were admitted.
Ventilator-associated pneumonia is the same type of infection in people on a breathing machine.
New fever, cough, and purulent (pus-like) sputum.
Falling oxygen levels, or a new shadow on a chest X-ray.
Sputum or breathing tube sample for culture.
Blood cultures and a chest X-ray.
Procalcitonin (a blood marker of bacterial infection), repeated over time.
Your team will choose antibiotics based on your risk of resistant germs and your cultures.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: You are in hospital, so let staff know about any new breathlessness or cough.
Your team will review your cultures and repeat tests after treatment starts.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Oxygen levels falling, or breathing very fast
Confusion, low blood pressure, or fainting
